extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and applicants for Research Project Grant (RPG) mechanisms (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34)
extracted.subtask_description: Standard definitions and considerations for reviewers evaluating NIH Research Project Grant applications (R01, R03, R15, R21, R34), including core review criteria and mechanism-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R01, R03, R21, R34: Reviewers provide an overall impact score reflecting likelihood to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the field, considering the listed review criteria and additional criteria as applicable. R15: Reviewers provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect likelihood for the project to make an important scientific contribution, provide research opportunities to students, and strengthen the institution's research environment, in consideration of the review criteria and additional criteria as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: R03 (Small Research Grant Program) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The R03 small grant supports discrete, well-defined projects that realistically can be completed in two years and that require limited levels of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the research project usually is limited, an R03 grant application may not contain extensive detail or discussion. Accordingly, reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach to the problem. Appropriate justification for the proposed work can be provided through literature citations, data from other sources, or from investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly in applications proposing pilot or feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: R15 (Academic Research Enhancement Award) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The objectives of the R15 program are to (1) provide support for meritorious research, (2) strengthen the research environment of schools that have not been major recipients of NIH support, and (3) expose available undergraduate and graduate students in such environments to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required for R15 application; however, they may be included if available. Reviewers should consider whether, if funded, the AREA award will have a substantial effect on the school/academic component in terms of strengthening the research environment and exposing students to research. For Investigator criterion, consider whether PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience in supervising students in research. For Environment, consider likely availability of well-qualified students and evidence that students have pursued or are likely to pursue careers in biomedical/behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental Research Grant Program) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The R21 exploratory/developmental grant supports investigation of novel scientific ideas or new model systems, tools, or technologies that have the potential for significant impact on biomedical or biobehavioral research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An R21 grant application need not have extensive background material or preliminary information. Accordingly, reviewers will focus their evaluation on the conceptual framework, the level of innovation, and the potential to significantly advance our knowledge or understanding. Appropriate justification may be provided through literature citations, data from other sources, or, when available, investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, but may be included if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: R34 (NIH Clinical Trial Planning Grant Program) guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH Clinical Trial Planning Grant Program (R34) supports development of Phase III clinical trials, including establishment of the research team, development of tools for data management and research oversight, definition of recruitment strategies, finalization of the protocol, and preparation of an operations/procedures manual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Clinical Trial Planning Grant is not designed for collection of preliminary data or conduct of pilot studies to support rationale for a clinical trial. Accordingly, reviewers will focus evaluation on the rationale for the proposed clinical trial and the design/protocol of the proposed trial in its current, early form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If the aims of the project are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R01, R03, R21, R34: Consider how successful completion of the aims will change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventative interventions that drive the field. R15: In addition to the above, consider whether the project will have a substantial effect on the school/academic component by strengthening the research environment and exposing students to research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project? If Early Stage Investigators or those in the early stages of independent careers, do they have appropriate experience and training? If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For collaborative or multi-PD/PI projects, evaluate whether investigators have complementary and integrated expertise and whether leadership approach, governance and organizational structure are appropriate. R15-specific: also consider whether PD(s)/PI(s) have suitable experience in supervising students in research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broad sense, and whether a refinement, improvement, or new application of such elements is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims of the project? Are potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success presented?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For early-stage projects, evaluate whether the strategy will establish feasibility and whether particularly risky aspects will be managed. If human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research are involved, assess plans to address: (1) protection of human subjects from research risks, and (2) inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, as well as inclusion (or exclusion) of children, justified in terms of scientific goals and research strategy. R15 variant: similar expectations; additionally consider whether the application provides sufficient evidence that the project can stimulate student interest in biomedical/behavioral science careers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional support, equipment and other physical resources available to investigators and whether the project will benefit from unique features of the scientific environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements. R15-specific: consider availability of well-qualified students to participate and evidence that students have pursued or are likely to pursue careers in the biomedical or behavioral sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: For research that involves human subjects but does not involve one of the six categories of research that are exempt under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and the proposed protections from research risk relating to their participation according to the following five review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five review criteria: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For research that involves human subjects and meets criteria for exemption under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee evaluates: (1) justification for the exemption, (2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and (3) sources of materials. See Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves human subjects and/or NIH-defined clinical research, the committee will evaluate the proposed plans for the inclusion (or exclusion) of individuals on the basis of sex/gender, race, and ethnicity, as well as the inclusion (or exclusion) of children to determine if it is justified in terms of the scientific goals and research strategy proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Guidelines for the Review of Inclusion in Clinical Research for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals as part of the scientific assessment according to the following five points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five points to assess: (1) proposed use of the animals, and species, strains, ages, sex, and numbers to be used; (2) justifications for the use of animals and for the appropriateness of the species and numbers proposed; (3) adequacy of veterinary care; (4) procedures for limiting discomfort, distress, pain and injury to that which is unavoidable in the conduct of scientifically sound research including the use of analgesic, anesthetic, and tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices; and (5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with the AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia. For additional information, refer to the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If needed, determine whether adequate protection is proposed (i.e., biosafety, containment, and related protections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For Resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate adequacy of responses to prior reviewer comments and whether changes appropriately address previous concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess accomplishments during the prior project period and whether the proposed renewal represents a logical and meritorious continuation or expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For Revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision application relates to a specific line of investigation presented in the original application that was not recommended for approval by the committee, consider whether the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through the use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the unique contributions and whether they represent added value beyond U.S.-based resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided in this section of the application regarding Select Agent(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess: (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used in the proposed research, (2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, (3) the procedures that will be used to monitor possession, use and transfer of Select Agent(s), and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the following Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing the following types of resources, are reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types of plans to consider: (1) Data Sharing Plan, (2) Sharing Model Organisms, and (3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS)/Genomic Data Sharing Plan. Evaluate whether the plans or rationales for not sharing are reasonable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess realism and justification of requested resources and time period relative to aims and proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this section to offer constructive guidance, suggestions for improvement, or explicit recommendations regarding resubmission.
